<translate>
<!--T:1-->
'''Publications''' are the literature of a catalogue: books, articles, exhibition catalogues, catalogues raisonnés, newspaper articles, brochures, videos and any other published work that discusses the artist or reproduces the works. Together they form the artist's '''bibliography''', and they are the sources the artworks cite. Unpublished letters, e-mails, certificates, invoices, manuscripts and diaries are not publications but sources of their own type; see [[Sources and citations]].

<!--T:2-->
Publications are shared: one book about three artists is a single record, linked to each of them. This page explains how a publication is recorded and connected. For the list of sections, see [[How openCR is structured/Records and their sections#Publications|Records and their sections]]; for every single field, see the [[Field reference]].

<!--T:3-->
== Before creating a publication ==
* '''Search first.''' The publication may already exist, entered for another artist. Use the existing record rather than creating a duplicate. If you may edit it, add your artist under [[#Related artists|Related artists]]; if it belongs only to artists of other catalogues, ask the platform administrator to add yours.
* '''Authors and publishers''' are [[Directory|directory]] entries. Create the ones you need first, so you can find them when you add the contributors.
* '''Choose the short name.''' The ''Alias'' is the publication's short name. The lists in which a publication is picked, for example when an artwork cites it, find it by its alias as well as by its title. Use a consistent pattern, such as author and year.

<!--T:4-->
== The main data ==
The main data of a publication are edited in a pop-up: in ''Edit Mode'', the pencil before the publication's ID opens ''Main data of the publication''. The form for a new publication applies the same checks. ''Type of publication'', ''Title'' and ''Alias'' are required. The fields come in six groups.

<!--T:18-->
=== Publication ===
* '''Type of publication''': the kind of publication. There are 23 kinds, among them Book, Article in magazine, Newspaper article, Exhibition Catalogue, Works Catalogue, Catalogue, Article in catalogue, Magazine, Brochure, Flyer, Thesis, Press release, Video, Audio and Internet (blog, review and similar). Pick the closest one; in the PRO menu, the bibliography can be filtered and sorted by it.
* '''Public (shown on open.cr)''': publishes the publication; leave it unticked until the record is complete. Internal remarks go into private notes on the publication's page (see [[Objects#Notes|notes]]).
* '''Authorized catalogue raisonné''': tick it only for the authorized catalogue raisonné. Lists then show a label after its title, and the publication's page after the type of publication.
* '''Alias''': the short name (see above). When another publication already has the same alias, the pop-up names it and asks for a different one; ''Save anyway'' keeps it all the same.
* '''Abbreviation''': a short citation form, such as ''[CabraDeLuna1992a]'', if the catalogue uses one. The page shows it in ''Edit Mode'' only.
* '''Reference''': a citation key or external reference code. The publication's page shows it, also to visitors.

<!--T:5-->
=== Title ===
* '''Title''' and '''Subtitle'''.
* '''Publication''': for an article or a contribution, the work it appears in, such as the magazine, newspaper or book. For a stand-alone book, leave it empty.
* '''Series''', shown on the publication's page.

<!--T:19-->
=== Date and place of publication ===
* '''Day''', '''Month''' and '''Year'''. Leave the day and month empty when unknown; never use January as a placeholder. A month needs a year, and a day needs a month.
* '''City''' and '''Country'''.

<!--T:20-->
=== Edition and extent ===
* '''Edition''': the edition statement as the title page writes it, such as ''7. Auflage''. Leave it empty for a book with only one edition. It is not the print run of a work of art.
* '''Volume''' and '''Total number of volumes'''. The volume cannot be higher than the total.
* '''Number of pages''' and '''Number of copies''' (the print run, if known). Empty or 0 means not known.

<!--T:6-->
=== Extract ===
When the record describes a specific extract rather than a whole work, such as an article, '''Page(s)''', '''Illustration''' and '''Coloured''' record its page or pages, the number of the illustration, and whether the illustration is in colour.

<!--T:21-->
=== ISBN, ISSN and link ===
'''ISBN''' for books, '''ISSN''' for magazines, and '''Link''': a web address of the publication or of its record, starting with http:// or https://.

<!--T:8-->
== Contributors ==
The '''Agents''' section of a publication lists everyone who contributed: author, editor, co-author, writer, journalist, publisher, gallery, organiser, sponsor and so on. Each entry points to a [[Directory|directory]] entry and gives the role.
* In ''Edit Mode'', the plus icon next to ''Agents'' opens a pop-up: search the directory by any part of the name, then choose the role and, if needed, the part. The pencil icon before an entry opens the same pop-up to change it; the bin icon after it removes that one role.
* A person can have several roles on the same publication, for example author and editor. Each role is entered once: openCR refuses the same person with the same role a second time.
* The byline shown with the publication is made up of the '''authors''', '''co-authors''', '''writers''', '''journalists''' and '''editors'''. Co-authors, writers and journalists carry their role in brackets, editors ''(ed.)''. Other roles, such as publisher or gallery, do not appear in it. Someone who is both author and editor appears in it twice.
* A contributor can be limited to one part of the publication: an essay, the introduction, the preface, the afterword and so on, chosen from the list or typed as a name. Leave this empty when the role applies to the whole publication. As each role is entered only once, someone who wrote both the preface and an essay is recorded once as author, without a part.

<!--T:9-->
== Related artists ==
'''Related artists''' lists the artists the publication is about. This is what puts a publication into an artist's bibliography: '''a publication without an entry here does not appear in the artist's bibliography''', even if it is public. The related artists also decide who may edit the publication: the editors of their catalogues.
* In ''Edit Mode'', the plus icon next to ''Related artists'' opens a pop-up that offers the artists you may edit and that are not related to the publication yet. The pencil before an entry changes its three settings; to relate another artist instead, remove the entry with the bin and add the other one.
* Removing the last related artist takes the publication out of every artist's bibliography, and afterwards only the platform administrator can edit it. The bin warns before it does so.

<!--T:10-->
Each entry has three independent settings:
{| class="wikitable"
! Setting !! Effect
|-
| '''Use in web''' || Read by the ''Usage'' filter of the publication lists in the PRO menu. It does not hide the publication: the bibliography on open.cr shows it either way.
|-
| '''Use in CR''' || The catalogue raisonné drafts print an artwork's references only from publications that have this ticked for the work's artist.
|-
| '''Use as reference in CR''' || Marks a reference publication of the catalogue. It is read by the ''Usage'' filter of the PRO lists.
|}
An entry added in the pop-up starts with ''Use in web'' and ''Use in CR'' ticked and ''Use as reference in CR'' unticked. A publication created with ''Easy publication creation'' gets its artist with ''Use in web'' and ''Use in CR'' unticked: tick ''Use in CR'' if the catalogue raisonné drafts should print its references. On the artist's page, ''Publications used as reference'' lists the artist's entries in ''References to artists'' (see below). In the public view, it shows a publication only when the publication is public and ''Use in web'' or ''Use in CR'' is ticked for that artist; in ''Edit Mode'', it shows every entry.

<!--T:11-->
When a publication discusses several artists on different pages, the pages per artist are recorded in '''References to artists'''. In ''Edit Mode'', its plus icon opens a pop-up with the artist, ''Page'', ''Illustration'', ''Reference'' and a ''Comment'', which the publication's page shows under the entry, also in the public view. An artist can have several entries. The same entries appear on the artist's page under ''Publications used as reference'' (in the public view only as described above), where they can be added and changed as well.

<!--T:12-->
== Events, languages and related publications ==
* '''Related events''': the events the publication documents, for example the exhibition an exhibition catalogue accompanies, with page and illustration references where useful. The pop-up searches events by name, venue, city, year or number.
* '''Used Languages''': the languages the publication is written in, each once. The pop-up lists the website languages first, then all languages. This describes the publication itself and has nothing to do with the languages of the openCR catalogue.
* '''Related Publications''': links to other publications: part of, version of, copy of, facsimile of, based on, preparatory for, derived from, similar to, related to. Enter each link once, on one of the two publications; the page of each shows the link from its own side. openCR refuses the same link a second time, in either direction, and a publication cannot be related to itself.

<!--T:13-->
== Artworks cited ==
The '''Referenced Objects''' section lists the artworks the publication mentions or illustrates, with their reference number, page, illustration number and illustration page. Each entry also records whether the illustration is in colour, which the artwork's bibliography shows. It is the same list as an [[Objects|artwork's]] bibliography, seen from the other side. When you work through a publication, ''Enter references in bulk'' adds its artworks one after another in a single pop-up.

<!--T:14-->
== Images ==
Images of the publication, such as its cover, are uploaded with the image upload and belong to the publication; the page shows them in its right-hand column, in ''Edit Mode'' under the heading ''Publication Images''. In ''Edit Mode'', the pencil of an image opens a pop-up for its ''Public'' tick, its description in each language and its photographer. Images of a publication shared by several artists are changed or deleted by the platform administrator.

<!--T:15-->
== Before publishing ==
* Type, title, date and place are complete, as far as they are known.
* Authors and editors are recorded with those roles.
* Each artist the publication is about is listed in ''Related artists''.
Then tick ''Public (shown on open.cr)'' in the main data.

<!--T:16-->
== Common pitfalls ==
* '''Duplicates.''' Before creating a publication, search for it; it may have been entered for another artist.
* '''Missing from the bibliography.''' When a publication does not appear in an artist's bibliography, check ''Related artists'' first: usually the artist's entry is missing. Otherwise, check that the publication is public.
* '''Empty byline.''' Only authors, co-authors, writers, journalists and editors appear in the byline. A text's author entered with another role, such as ''organiser'', does not.
* '''Title and containing work mixed up.''' For an article, the article's title goes into ''Title'', the magazine or book into ''Publication''.
* '''Mirror relations.''' A relation between two publications is entered once.
